articles.title: ClassNK Releases Second Edition of Cyber Security Management Guidelines
articles.summary: ClassNK has released the second edition of its "Guidelines for Cyber Security Management System for Ships." Intended for shipowners and ship management companies, the guidelines set out the requirements for a Cyber Security Management System (CSMS)…
articles.body: ClassNK Releases Second Edition of Cyber Security Management Guidelines Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 30, 2026 © ClassNK ClassNK has released the second edition of its "Guidelines for Cyber Security Management System for Ships." Intended for shipowners and ship management companies, the guidelines set out the requirements for a Cyber Security Management System (CSMS), through which a Company addresses the cyber risks associated with ship operations as part of its day-to-day work, from governance and responsibilities ashore and onboard to the technical controls applied to shipboard systems. The Guidelines also make ClassNK’s certification audits transparent by showing the assessment criteria applied in them. In audits, ClassNK looks at the governance behind a company’s cyber security: policy and management commitment, defined roles and responsibilities, risk assessment, implementation and operation of controls, and preparedness for incidents. The second edition has been restructured with reference to ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27002, and the assessment criteria for each CSMS requirement have been clarified. The requirements have also been mapped to the cyber security requirements of major vetting schemes. Cyber security is increasingly covered in the external assessments conducted by maritime stakeholders, and many of those requirements focus on how cyber risk is managed. A CSMS certified against these guidelines gives companies an objective means of demonstrating that governance to external stakeholders, and a single foundation for responding to multiple vetting requirements. Background The IMO recommends that cyber risks be managed within the Safety Management Systems under the ISM Code. In response, ClassNK published the first edition of the Guidelines in 2019, setting out CSMS requirements built on the framework of the ISM Code, and has since been providing CSMS certification based on the guidelines. As a collective effort of the International Association of Classification Societies (IACS), the application of IACS UR E26 and E27 has defined the cyber resilience capabilities that ships and their onboard systems must have from the newbuild phase. At the same time, a vessel’s operating environment keeps changing throughout its service life, as the systems are updated and operations and organizations change. Addressing cyber risks is therefore not a matter of technical measures alone; continuous management is essential to select, implement, maintain and review those measures appropriately. In recent years, cyber risk management covering practices such as access control, software updates, education and training, and incident response have also become a part of the assessment criteria as part of the subject to the schemes established by DryBMS, OCIMF, RightShip and others, each with their own criteria. The first edition offered the elements for establishing a CSMS as a high-level objective, leaving each Company to interpret how to achieve them within its own organization. Putting those elements into practice requires wide efforts across the whole Company, from shore-based organizations to shipboard operations, and time to achieve. Through its audits since 2019, ClassNK has built up practical knowledge of what effective implementation looks like. Drawing on that experience, the second edition makes clear what is verified in audits and has been designed with other external assessments in mind, so that a CSMS built on the guidelines also prepares a company to meet them. Main revisions Clarification of audit criteria, structured with reference to international standards The guidelines now consist of two parts: Part 1 sets out the CSMS requirements, and Part 2 specifies the audit criteria and the objective evidence required for each requirement. This allows companies to understand in advance what will be verified in audits and prepare accordingly, and makes it easier to identify where there is room for improvement in their own practices. Mapping to external assessment criteria set by major industry bodies The assessment criteria in Part 2 have also been mapped against the cyber security requirements or benchmarks of major vetting bodies (covering RISQ, SIRE 2.0, DryBMS and TMSA*3). Rather than interpreting each scheme separately, Companies can use the CSMS as a common framework for meeting them and can expect the reduction of the time and burden needed for compliance. ClassNK will continue to support cyber security efforts in the maritime industry through the provision of guidelines as well as audits and certification. How to access guidelines The guidelines are available to download via "Guidelines" of My Page on ClassNK’s website after registration: ClassNK MyPage Login

articles.title: Corn Belt Ports See Notable Freight Tonnage Growth in 2026
articles.summary: In the most recent annual report released by the U.S. Waterborne Commerce Statistics Center, two Corn Belt Ports regions took top honors for showing some of the highest growth rates in the inland waterway port system. The Mid-America Port Commission (IL…
articles.body: Corn Belt Ports See Notable Freight Tonnage Growth in 2026 Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 30, 2026 © Corn Belt Ports In the most recent annual report released by the U.S. Waterborne Commerce Statistics Center, two Corn Belt Ports regions took top honors for showing some of the highest growth rates in the inland waterway port system. The Mid-America Port Commission (IL, MO, IA), established in 1999, was ranked as the 40th largest port in the U.S., and saw a 15.2% growth in freight tonnage during the 2024 reporting year (published 2026). This is the highest growth rate for any large (Top 50) U.S. Inland Port. The Illinois Waterway Ports Commission established in 2023, and now reported as a port statistical area in the report, saw a 5.9% increase in freight tonnage, the largest increase of any port statistical area in the U.S. In the report the Upper Mississippi River (Marine Highway 35) saw a 4.2% increase, and the Illinois River (Marine Highway 55 NORTH) saw a 1.2% increase in freight tonnage overall. The Corn Belt Ports are special districts of government or official government collaborations. They are the modern, sustainable, rural, regional, inland, partnership ports on the Upper Mississippi River (Marine Highway 35) and the Illinois River (Marine Highway 35 NORTH) inside of the lock and dam system recognized by the U.S. Congress as the Upper Mississippi River and Illinois Waterway System. The Corn Belt Ports consist of the Illinois Waterway Ports Commission, the Mid-America Port Commission, the Upper Mississippi River Ports of Eastern lowa and Western Illinois, and the Northern Grain Belt Ports. While Bozhong 26-6 oilfield continued to expand production capacity, effectively bolstering energy supply capacity in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei and Bohai Rim regions, the firm explained that Panyu 10-4 oilfield achieved fully automated operations through intelligent systems and significantly reduced carbon dioxide emissions by applying a power generation system that recovers waste heat from produced water. The three firm ships, valued at a combined CNY1.575bn (about $235m), remain on order at subsidiary Tangshan Dajin, with completion scheduled across 2029 and 2030. The original deal carried a maximum value of CNY2.1bn ($313m) if the additional ship was declared. The yard said the decision does not constitute a contractual breach or trigger penalties. Dajin also expects no material impact on its production schedule or 2026 financial performance. The Chinese group did not identify the customer in its filing. However, Chinese shipbuilding market reports have linked the contract to Kriton Lendoudis-led Evalend Shipping. Splash covered the original agreement in July when Evalend emerged as the reported buyer of the three-plus-one series, marking the Greek owner’s entry into the newcastlemax sector. The group has since been linked to further tanker and bulk carrier investments in Asia, including a quartet of LR1 product tankers at Yangzijiang Shipbuilding. Other Greek owners have also turned to Dajin for newcastlemax tonnage. John Coustas-led Danaos Corporation has four 211,000 dwt vessels on order for delivery in 2028, while the Adrianopoulos family’s Cape Shipping has booked a pair of the same size for 2029 in a deal worth around $153m. The two programmes represent a combined investment of about $450m. articles.body: Interconnectors October 30, 2026 · 1 day ago €3.1 billion Spain-France interconnector is 70% complete NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Red Eléctrica The multibillion-euro Biscay Gulf interconnector, set to increase electricity exchange capacity between Spain and France from 2.8 GW to 5 GW, is 70% complete, with onshore cable laying currently underway. Spanish transmission system operator (TSO) Red Eléctrica has begun underground cable laying for the electrical interconnection project that will, across the Bay of Biscay, connect Gatika in Spain and France's Cubnezais. The underground HVDC cables will run for 13 kilometers, from the Gatika converter station to the coast at Lemoiz, where they will connect to the submarine cables. Furthermore, Red Eléctrica recently completed the second phase of subsea cable laying, a 50-kilometer stretch, using Prysmian's cable-laying vessel (CLV) Monna Lisa. On the Biscayan coast, the first phase was completed in August with NKT's CLV Victoria, which was responsible for installing the first 65 kilometers of the route. With this, all the submarine cables have been installed in the Biscay section of the submarine interconnection. Work will continue on the sections off the coast of Gipuzkoa between November and February, with all sections expected to be laid in French waters until the summer. The Spanish TSO also reported that the construction of the future Gatika converter station is progressing well, with civil engineering work completed and the electromechanical assembly currently underway. The Biscay Gulf interconnector is now 70% complete. Developed by Red Eléctrica and its French counterpart RTE, through the joint venture Inelfe, the project is considered a Project of Common Interest by the European Union and is co-financed through CINEA - the European Union's Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency, in addition to support from the European Investment Bank (EIB). articles.body: Ports and Logistics Dockworkers unite across 113 ports in global anti-war protest Sam Chambers October 30, 2026 0 2,326 1 minute read CGT CGT One of the largest coordinated port labour mobilisations in history is underway today, with more than 25 unions staging strikes and demonstrations at 113 ports across 22 countries and territories. The worldwide action, organised under the banner “Dockworkers do not work for war”, has expanded dramatically from a smaller mobilisation involving 20 ports across seven countries in February. Major gateways involved include Hamburg, Le Havre, Marseille, Genoa, Gioia Tauro, Piraeus, Tangier Med, Mersin and India’s Nhava Sheva. France’s CGT has called a 24-hour walkout across approximately 24 ports, predicting that as much as 95% of national port activity could be halted. Italy has registered a nationwide 24-hour ports strike, coinciding with a general strike affecting other transport sectors. In Greece, seafarers’ unions have called 24-hour stoppages expected to disrupt ferry services at Piraeus, Rafina, Lavrio, Patras and Igoumenitsa. Organisers estimate that participating unions represent workers handling around 40% of Mediterranean container traffic, with up to 40,000 containers potentially delayed.< However, the actual disruption remains uncertain. Some ports are holding demonstrations rather than stopping cargo operations, while Genoa’s port authority anticipates relatively limited disruption. The campaign primarily opposes military cargo shipments through civilian ports, alongside demands for improved wages, working conditions and protections against automation. Although unprecedented in scale for this particular campaign, claims that it is the world’s largest port strike remain unverified. An international solidarity campaign for Liverpool dockworkers in January 1997 involved 105 ports and cities across 27 countries. No further worldwide coordinated strike date has been announced. Separately, a potential November 1 strike involving 250 port watchmen threatens operations at Los Angeles and Long Beach, although negotiations to avert the stoppage are continuing. Italy also faces another national general strike on November 20.
